ga-county-commission-district-lines.area: Georgia — the 30 counties whose commission district map is not drawn, and Richmond's super districts
ga-county-commission-district-lines.summary: In 30 counties the map does not draw the commission districts, so it cannot say which one you are in; the County card names the whole commission there. Elsewhere the district card names your commissioner.
ga-county-commission-district-lines.why: This app draws a county's map only when its district elections confirm it. These maps disagree with a contest, or no contest voted in one district alone has tested them.
ga-county-commission-district-lines.wanted: Each county's current commission district map, as its election office uses it.

ga-county-commission-members.summary: The County card names the commissioners elected since November 2024 and lists the seats filled before then with no one in them.
ga-county-commission-members.why: No state office publishes who sits on Georgia's county commissions, so this app names them from the state's election results, which carry county races only from November 2024 on.
ga-county-commission-members.wanted: Each county's own list of its commissioners and the district each one represents, with its current district map.

ga-municipal-officeholders.summary: The City or Town card names the place and says when a city and its county are one government, and not who your mayor and council are.
ga-municipal-officeholders.why: No statewide list of Georgia's mayors and council members has been read for this app, and no city's own pages have been read yet.
ga-municipal-officeholders.wanted: A statewide roster of every city's and town's mayor and council members by district, or each place's own published list.

ga-precinct-lines-since-2024.area: Georgia — the 50 counties whose ballots since November 2024 do not match the 2024 precinct map
ga-precinct-lines-since-2024.summary: In 50 counties a precinct line may be out of date, because the county's ballots since November 2024 do not match the 2024 map this app draws. The precinct card says so in those counties.
ga-precinct-lines-since-2024.why: The newest statewide precinct map this app has found is the General Assembly's for 2024, and counties have changed their precincts since then.
ga-precinct-lines-since-2024.wanted: Each county's current precinct map, or a statewide precinct map newer than the 2024 one.

ga-school-board-district-lines.area: Georgia — the 48 county school boards whose district map is not drawn, the 7 with no map, and the city school systems
ga-school-board-district-lines.summary: For 55 county school boards and every city school system, the map does not draw board districts, so it cannot say which one you are in. Elsewhere the district card names your board member.
ga-school-board-district-lines.why: This app draws a county's map only when its district elections confirm it. These maps disagree with a contest, or no contest voted in one district alone has tested them, and city systems' maps are not published with the counties'.
ga-school-board-district-lines.wanted: Each school system's current board district map, as its election office uses it.

ga-school-board-members.summary: A county school system's card names the board members elected since November 2024 and lists the seats filled before then with no one in them. City systems' boards are not named.
ga-school-board-members.why: No statewide list of Georgia's school board members is published, so this app names county boards from the state's election results, which carry county races only from November 2024 on.
ga-school-board-members.wanted: Each school system's own list of its board members and the district each one represents, with its current district map.

ga-superior-court-appointments.summary: The Judicial Circuit card names each judge and district attorney chosen at the seat's last election. Anyone the governor appointed since is not shown, and West Georgia's district attorney is not named until it holds its first election.
ga-superior-court-appointments.why: No current list of Georgia's superior court judges and district attorneys, with the date each took office, has been found that this app can read, so it names them from the state's election results.
ga-superior-court-appointments.wanted: A list of each circuit's sitting judges and district attorney that says who was appointed and when, kept current by the court system or the prosecutors' council.

ga-superior-court-held-back.area: Georgia — the Alcovy, Atlantic, Cobb, Griffin, Paulding and Waycross circuits
ga-superior-court-held-back.summary: In a few circuits the card names no one for a judge's seat or the district attorney, because the state court system's directory lists the seat's last winner in another office of that circuit. The card says who and why.
ga-superior-court-held-back.why: The election results and the court system's directory disagree about these people, and neither carries a date that says which is newer.
ga-superior-court-held-back.wanted: A dated record of the change: a judge's retirement, or a district attorney's appointment to the bench and the appointment of a successor.
